title: Higher-level streaming chat operator pattern + lightweight hooks for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Teams using the Python SDK ask for a compact, high-level consumer API for streaming chat completions that reduces boilerplate while preserving control for advanced patterns (per-message acking, cancel propagation, soft-fallbacks). Current low-level event iterators are powerful but require repetitive glue: signal propagation, error classification, per-message telemetry, and simple retry/soft-fallback wiring.

Goal: Deliver an operator-style facade for streaming chat that: (1) exposes a concise context manager + callback hook surface for common use cases; (2) allows composable cancellation and graceful shutdown semantics; (3) provides explicit telemetry hooks per token/fragment/message; (4) integrates with existing retry/backoff policies at a single attachment point; (5) ships with cookbook examples showing best practices and migration path from the iterator APIs.

Proposal summary: Add a new class ChatStreamOperator and a small hooks protocol (on_open, on_token, on_message, on_error, on_close). The operator is a higher-level wrapper around the existing event iterator: it manages lifecycle, captures per-message timing and bytes emitted, exposes explicit cancellation tokens, and surfaces a single attach_point for retry and fallback policies. The default operator will be opinionated: buffered message assembly with a small sliding window for latency-sensitive apps and optional exact-stream mode for deterministic token-level consumers.

API sketch:
- ChatStreamOperator(response_iterable, *, mode="buffered", telemetry_hook=None, retry_policy=None)
- with ChatStreamOperator(...) as op:
    for message in op.messages():
       # application-level message handling
- Hooks: on_open(metadata), on_token(token, meta), on_message(message, meta), on_error(err, meta), on_close(summary)

Design decisions:
- Provide a single retry attachment that can synthesize a short soft-fallback (e.g., retry on idempotent partial-stream errors then fall back to non-streaming completion). This keeps app code simple while enabling safe recovery.
- Default "buffered" mode will emit assembled messages (application common path). Exact-token mode remains available for advanced users.
- Expose a cancel() method on operator that coordinates upstream cancel requests, drains in-flight tokens up to a configurable timeout, and emits a final on_close with a complemented summary.
- Telemetry hook receives per-token and per-message timing and counts, enabling fine-grained cost/latency breakdowns without requiring the app to instrument the iterator.

Migration: Provide a small compatibility shim that accepts an existing event iterator and returns a ChatStreamOperator wrapping it; include snippet in migration guide.

Testing plan: Unit tests for hook invocation order, cancel semantics, soft-fallback correctness; integration tests against staging runtime with injected partial-stream errors; fuzz tests for interleaved token/message boundaries.

Rollout: Feature gated behind python-sdk v1.9 feature flag. Dogfood in internal chat-app microservice for 2 weeks, collect telemetry, then enable for customers.

Security/Privacy: Operator does not change payloads; when telemetry_hook is provided it will be documented that PII must be redacted upstream.
acceptance_criteria: New ChatStreamOperator class implemented and exported from redwood.sdk.streaming.chat
Hooks protocol implemented: on_open, on_token, on_message, on_error, on_close
Cancel method coordinates with underlying iterator and honors drain timeout (configurable)
Single retry_attachment point implemented and documented with at least one soft-fallback policy example
Unit + integration test coverage: >= 90% lines for operator module; deterministic tests for hook ordering
Migration example and cookbook added to docs site and python SDK repo examples/streaming_operator.md
Feature-flag gating working and dogfood run completed with telemetry dashboard linked
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Triage complete. Priority P1 because this reduces large amount of duplicated glue in several internal services and will improve reliability. Assigned to Diego.

2026-03-03 - Diego Morales: Spiked an implementation wrapping the current event iterator. Basic on_token/on_message hook flow works. Pushed draft PR for early feedback: github.com/redwood/py-sdk/pull/1892
2026-03-05 - PM review (Ravi Singh): Request to ensure retry_attachment can call a user-provided policy that decides between retrying streaming vs falling back to a non-streaming call. Added to ACs.

2026-03-06 - Design review (Maya Chen): Prefer default buffered mode to assemble message-level semantics. Exact-token mode should be opt-in. Suggested adding a simple boolean "emit_partial_messages" to control sliding-window emission. Incorporating feedback.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Implemented cancel() with configurable drain_timeout Ms. Added tests for cancel while tokens are streaming; found a race condition when iterator raises in-flight EOF — fixed by serializing on_close emission.

2026-03-09 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Integration test with staging runtime injected partial-stream disconnects shows operator correctly triggers retry_attachment and emits on_error then on_close. Need to add perf test for telemetry hook overhead.
2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Addressed perf test by batching telemetry hook calls per-message instead of per-token when telemetry_hook.report_batch=True. Updated docs and PR. Ready for Review.
2026-03-12 - Code review (SRE: Priya Raman): Ensure operator honors contextlib context manager cancellation on SIGTERM in dogfood service. Added small runtime shim in examples for graceful shutdown.
